summary: This standards-track memo defines M3UA, a protocol for carrying SS7 MTP3-user signalling such as ISUP and SCCP messages over IP using SCTP. It is used between a Signalling Gateway and a Media Gateway Controller or IP database, or between IP applications. It replaces RFC 3332.

eli5.summary: Old telephone networks have their own language for setting up calls. This lets that language travel inside internet packets, so phone systems and computers can talk to each other.

questions: how does ss7 work over ip
subtitle: How telephone signalling (SS7 MTP3 users such as ISUP and SCCP) is carried over IP using SCTP.

tldr.problem: Telephone networks signal with SS7, but call controllers and databases increasingly live on IP networks, so SS7 user parts such as ISUP and SCCP need a way to reach them without a local MTP3 layer.
tldr.mechanism: M3UA lets a Signalling Gateway terminate SS7 MTP2 and MTP3 and carry the MTP3-user messages and MTP network management events over SCTP to Application Server Processes, using routing keys, a small set of message classes and ASP and AS state machines.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4666 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3332; it defines the protocol, its procedures and its failover and load-sharing modes.

today: RFC 4666 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3332. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 4666 defines the MTP3-User Adaptation Layer (M3UA). It supports the transport of any SS7 MTP3-user signalling, for example ISUP and SCCP messages, over IP using the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP). It also provides protocol elements so that MTP3-user peers in the SS7 and IP domains operate seamlessly.

The protocol is used between a Signalling Gateway (SG) and a Media Gateway Controller (MGC) or IP-resident database, or between two IP-based applications. The SG receives SS7 signalling over a standard SS7 interface and terminates SS7 MTP2 and MTP3. It then delivers ISUP, SCCP or other MTP3-user messages, and certain MTP network management events, over SCTP associations.

The delivery mechanism is expected to cover transfer of all MTP3-user messages, management of SCTP associations, process failover and load sharing, and asynchronous status reporting to management.
sections.eli5: A big phone company has gear that speaks an old signalling language. M3UA lets that language ride on internet connections so new computer-based call systems can join in.

sections.title: Roles and Where M3UA Sits
sections.content:
The SG appears to the SS7 network as an SS7 signalling point. It contains one or more Signalling Gateway Processes (SGPs). On the IP side, an Application Server (AS) is a logical entity serving a specific Routing Key, such as a virtual switch handling all call processing for a signalling relation. It contains one or more Application Server Processes (ASPs), of which one or more is normally active. An IP Server Process (IPSP) is like an ASP but uses M3UA in a point-to-point fashion and does not use a Signalling Gateway.

M3UA gives the upper layer on an ASP the same primitives that MTP3 gives its local users: MTP-TRANSFER, MTP-PAUSE, MTP-RESUME and MTP-STATUS. The ISUP or SCCP layer is therefore unaware that MTP3 services are provided remotely. M3UA does not itself provide MTP3 services. Unlike MTP Level 2, it does not impose a 272-octet limit on the signalling information field, though an SG must respect that limit when interworking with an SS7 network that cannot carry larger blocks.

SCTP is the recommended transport. Under certain scenarios, such as back-to-back connections without redundancy requirements, TCP MAY be used. By default the SGP acts as server and the ASP as client, so ASPs SHOULD initiate the SCTP association. The registered SCTP and TCP port is 2905.
sections.eli5: The gateway is a border post between the old phone country and the internet country. Workers behind it (the ASPs) take turns handling the messages, and the post decides who gets which message.

sections.title: Routing Keys and Routing Contexts
sections.content:
A Routing Key is a set of SS7 parameters and values that define the range of signalling traffic handled by one Application Server. Possible ingredients are the OPC, DPC and service indicator from the MTP3 routing label, and examples include the DPC alone or the DPC and OPC together. None of these is mandated. A Routing Context is a 4-octet value associated one to one with a Routing Key, and works like an index into the SGP's message distribution table.

An SGP can learn Routing Keys through static configuration or through the optional dynamic registration messages (REG REQ and DEREG REQ). When a message matches no key, the treatment is implementation dependent: it may go to a default AS or be dropped with a notification to layer management. In the other direction, an ASP picks an SGP by observing the destination point code, and possibly the SLS value, and must consider whether the related Routing Context is active.

The Network Appearance parameter identifies the SS7 network context where one SG serves several SS7 networks, since the same point code value may be reused in different networks. Its value is of local significance only.
sections.eli5: A routing key is a rule like: all letters addressed to this street go to this office. The routing context is the short number the offices use to refer to each rule.

sections.title: Message Format
sections.content:
Every M3UA message has a common header followed by zero or more parameters. The header holds the version (value 1 means Release 1.0), a reserved byte that SHOULD be zero, a message class, a message type and a 32-bit message length. The length counts the header and any parameter padding. All fields are in network byte order.

Parameters use a tag-length-value layout. A 16-bit tag identifies the parameter, a 16-bit length covers tag, length and value but not padding, and each parameter is padded with zero octets to a multiple of 4. Common parameters use tags in the range 0x00 to 0x3f, for example Routing Context (0x0006), Heartbeat Data (0x0009), Traffic Mode Type (0x000b), Error Code (0x000c), Status (0x000d) and ASP Identifier (0x0011). M3UA-specific tags run from 0x0200 to 0x02ff, for example Network Appearance (0x0200) and Protocol Data (0x0210).

The DATA message carries the original MTP3 message in the mandatory Protocol Data parameter: OPC, DPC, service indicator, network indicator, message priority, SLS and the user protocol data. The optional Network Appearance, if present, MUST be the first parameter because it defines the format of Protocol Data. MTP3 management messages such as TFP or TFA MUST NOT be carried as DATA payload. The SG terminates them and generates M3UA messages instead. DATA MUST NOT be sent on SCTP stream 0, while ASPSM, MGMT and RKM messages SHOULD use stream 0 (except BEAT, BEAT Ack and NTFY).
sections.eli5: Every M3UA message has a small label on the front saying what kind it is and how long it is. Inside are labelled boxes, each padded so it fits neatly into a slot.

sections.title: ASP and Application Server States
sections.content:
The SGP tracks the state of each ASP in each AS. An ASP is in one of three states. ASP-DOWN means the peer is unavailable or the SCTP association is down, and is the initial state. ASP-INACTIVE means the peer is available but application traffic is stopped. ASP-ACTIVE means traffic flows for a given Routing Context or set of contexts.

The ASP Up message moves an ASP from down to inactive, ASP Active moves it to active, ASP Inactive moves it back and ASP Down or loss of the SCTP association returns it to down. The SGP MUST answer ASP Up with ASP Up Ack even if the ASP is already inactive.

The AS itself has four states: AS-DOWN, AS-INACTIVE, AS-ACTIVE and AS-PENDING. When the last active ASP leaves, the AS goes to AS-PENDING, a recovery timer T(r) SHOULD start and incoming messages SHOULD be queued. If an ASP becomes active before T(r) expires, the queued messages are sent to it. Otherwise the AS moves to AS-INACTIVE or AS-DOWN and the queue may be discarded.

For IPSPs, an implementation MUST support the Single Exchange model and MAY implement the Double Exchange model.
sections.eli5: Workers can be off duty, waiting at the desk, or busy serving customers. If the last busy worker leaves, the shop holds the letters for a short while in case someone comes back.

sections.title: Traffic Modes, Network Management and Heartbeats
sections.content:
When an ASP sends ASP Active it names a Traffic Mode Type: Override (1), Loadshare (2) or Broadcast (3). In Override, the ASP takes over all traffic in the AS (primary and backup operation). In Loadshare it shares traffic with other active ASPs. In Broadcast it receives the same messages as any other active ASP. These modes SHOULD NOT be mixed within one Routing Context. The failover model is "n+k", where n ASPs are the minimum needed to carry traffic and k can take over, with "1+1" and "1+0" as subsets.

SS7 network management is mapped onto SSNM messages. DUNA says destinations are unreachable, DAVA says they are reachable, DAUD lets an ASP audit their state, SCON signals congestion, DUPU says a remote user part is unavailable and DRST reports restricted destinations. Affected point codes carry a mask that wildcards the low-order bits, so a whole cluster or region can be reported at once.

The optional heartbeat procedure is for transports that lack their own heartbeat. A peer that gets BEAT MUST answer with BEAT Ack, echoing any Heartbeat Data unchanged. If nothing arrives within 2*T(beat), the peer is considered unavailable.

Errors are reported with the ERR message and a 32-bit Error Code, for example Invalid Version (0x01), Unsupported Message Class (0x03), Unexpected Message (0x06), Invalid Routing Context (0x19) and No Configured AS for ASP (0x1a). The NTFY message reports AS state changes and events such as ASP failure.
sections.eli5: Workers can split the mail between them, or one can take over completely, or everyone can get a copy. The gateway also tells the computers when a phone route is blocked or busy so they stop sending down it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security section is short. Implementations MUST follow the normative guidance of RFC 3788 on the integration and use of security mechanisms in SIGTRAN protocols. M3UA itself does not define its own security mechanism in this section.

The overview also lists, among the reasons to prefer SCTP, its resistance to flooding and masquerade attacks.
sections.eli5: The rule is simple: follow the separate security guide written for this family of protocols, and do not invent your own locks.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
This document contains no new IANA actions; the subsections are retained for historical purposes. IANA assigned the SCTP Payload Protocol Identifier value 3 for M3UA. It SHOULD be included in each SCTP DATA chunk, and 0 (unspecified) is also allowed. IANA also registered port 2905 for SCTP, UDP and TCP, and SGPs are recommended to listen there, though they MAY use statically configured ports.

New message classes, message types and parameters are assigned through IETF Consensus. An implementation that receives an unsupported message type MUST respond with an Error message (Unsupported Message Type).
sections.eli5: The numbers other people need, such as the port and the protocol label, are already registered in a public list, so nobody has to guess them.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: SHOULD be zero and ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Message Class
fields.desc: Management, Transfer, SSNM, ASPSM, ASPTM or RKM.

fields.name: Message Length
fields.desc: Length in octets including the header and any parameter padding.

items.label: SSNM
items.desc: SS7 signalling network management: DUNA, DAVA, DAUD, SCON, DUPU, DRST.

items.label: ASPSM
items.desc: ASP state maintenance: ASP Up, ASP Down, Heartbeat and acknowledgements.

items.label: ASPTM
items.desc: ASP traffic maintenance: ASP Active, ASP Inactive and acknowledgements.

items.label: RKM
items.desc: Routing key management: registration and deregistration (optional).
